subject: Re: HeliosMed private cluster - p99 spikes & 504s (exec attention requested)
messages:
From: Priya Shah <pshah@heliosmed.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anand Iyer <a.iyer@heliosmed.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production: sporadic p99 latency spikes and 504s on private cluster

Hi Chloe,

We started seeing intermittent p99 spikes and a growing number of 504s in our on-prem private cluster this morning (first observed ~00:40 local). The pattern looks correlated with a nightly EMR ingestion batch — multiple patient record lookups time out which is causing downstream retries. Attaching a sample of request IDs and a compressed set of logs.

What we've observed: 
- p50 stable ~120ms, p95 ~420ms, p99 up to 6.2s
- 504s appear for ~4–8% of requests during bursts (duration 3–7 minutes)
- No recent code deploys on our side; we did apply a config adjustment to nginx LB at 00:05 but don't think that should affect internal node-to-node paths

We're on a strict processing window today — this needs urgent triage. Can your team start an investigation and propose a short-term mitigation? We'll keep Ops Pager open.

Attachments: helios_logs_20280115.zip (logs + sample trace ids)

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Director of Platform Ops, HeliosMed
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@heliosmed.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sporadic p99 latency spikes and 504s on private cluster

Priya — thanks for the data and the clear summary. We're opening a dedicated triage channel now.

Immediate plan: 
1) Dev and I will pull node-level metrics and KV cache hit rates (Dev, can you confirm access to the HeliosMed Prometheus endpoint?)
2) We'll attempt a non-disruptive cache warm and observe for one ingestion window
3) If the pattern persists, we will propose a temporary scaling/traffic-shift to reduce tail latency and book a maintenance window for any kernel-level changes

I'll keep this thread as the single source of truth and loop in leadership if impact grows. ETA for initial findings: 45–60 minutes.

-Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: (internal)
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sporadic p99 latency spikes and 504s on private cluster

I've started pulling the telemetry. Initial signs: elevated KV cache miss rate on the hot prefix during ingestion window, and NVMe IO flats on two worker nodes. Possible root causes to explore: 
- KV cache eviction caused by a configuration change (TTL/prefetch)
- IO queue depth saturation on NVMe (we see high svc time around the 00:40 spikes)
- A tail-heavy sequence length pattern from ingestion that blows through the K/V cache

I've attached a short runbook excerpt that outlines the non-disruptive cache-warm procedure and the commands I'll run to snapshot disk queue stats. If we need a hotpatch, I have a kpatch candidate that tunes queue_depth and raises ulimit for the inference process; that would require a brief rolling restart (per node).

Attachments: runbook_kvcache_snippet.pdf

- Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: HeliosMed private cluster — request for executive awareness and guidance

Laura/Markus — looping you in given HeliosMed is requesting an update to their platform leadership. Impact summary: 
- Incident: intermittent p99 latency spikes (up to 6.2s) and 504s during nightly EMR ingestion windows over the past 24 hours
- Customer impact: ingestion backfills failing; approx 4–8% of requests return 504s for short bursts; customer has flagged downstream SLA breach risk
- Initial tech findings: elevated KV cache miss rate + NVMe IO saturation on two worker nodes; possible config regression on cache TTL or prefetch

We need: 
1) Exec guidance on short-term mitigations we can propose (credit/SLA posture, capacity increase, fallback to degraded model)
2) Approval to schedule a rolling kernel/io tunable patch during their low-traffic window (Wed 01/18 02:00–03:00 local) if triage recommends it
3) A decision owner for customer communications (Camila suggested she will own comms)

Attaching triage notes and logs to the JIRA ticket, but want to ensure leadership is aware and ready to mobilize if this grows.

-Chloe
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 09:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: HeliosMed private cluster — request for executive awareness and guidance

Thanks for the heads-up Chloe. Quick thoughts: 
- Customer risk: High — this impacts EMR ingestion which is core to HeliosMed's operations. We should be prepared to offer a one-off SLA credit if the root cause is on our stack.
- Short-term mitigations to propose to customer now: 
  * Increase worker count by 2 during ingestion window (estimate ~2 hours to scale + validation)
  * Enable degraded-model fallback for non-critical queries to reduce tail load if applicable
  * If IO saturation confirmed, schedule rolling kernel tunable patch and provide a maintenance ETA

Please prepare a short impact/ask doc for me; I can pull budget sign-off for credits if needed but need a firm remediation ETA and rollback plan. Markus — can you confirm the risk of the proposed kpatch?

- Laura
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2028 14:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed mitigation and maintenance plan for HeliosMed private cluster

Team — results from two ingestion windows: KV cache warm reduced p99 in micro-tests but production still shows spikes tied to NVMe service time peaks on worker-07 and worker-09. Recommended plan: 

A) Immediate (within 2 hours): 
- Temporarily add +2 worker instances and shift 30% of traffic away from affected nodes (non-disruptive, no customer config changes)
- Continue cache-warm for hot prefixes during ingestion

B) Scheduled maintenance (Wed 01/18 02:00–03:30 local): 
- Rolling kpatch to adjust NVMe queue_depth and ulimits on inference process
- Per-node restart after patch (rolling, one node at a time)
- Post-patch smoke tests and 1 ingestion window monitoring

Risk & rollback: immediate rollback by removing kpatch and restoring previous queue_depth; we will keep +2 workers active for 24 hours as mitigation. Estimated customer-visible downtime: none; short tail improvements expected within first ingestion window after patch.

Attachments: kpatch_504_mitigation.diff, node-metrics-snapshot-0116.csv

- Dev
From: Priya Shah <pshah@heliosmed.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed mitigation and maintenance plan for HeliosMed private cluster

Chloe / Dev — thank you for the quick triage. We will accept the maintenance window on Wed 01/18 02:00–03:30 local and have Ops on standby. A couple of asks before you proceed: 
- Can you confirm whether this will trigger any SLA credit discussion? Our legal/compliance team has flagged a risk of late delivery for a regulatory submission if ingestion is delayed further.
- Please share an explicit smoke test checklist we can run post-patch.

Also: our internal logs show the pattern starts precisely after 00:40, which aligns with the nightly batch scheduler kicking off. We're sharing a copy of their scheduler logs to correlate.

Regards,
Priya
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@heliosmed.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 10:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed mitigation and maintenance plan for HeliosMed private cluster

Priya — closing the loop here with the agreed actions and links: 
- Maintenance window confirmed: Wed 01/18 02:00–03:30 local (rolling). Redwood will own the patch and post-patch validation.
- SLA posture: Laura has authorized us to offer a goodwill credit if the root cause is within our stack; formal credit amount will be decided after post-incident review (we'll propose a one-time credit and expedite the review).
- Smoke test checklist: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/HeliosMed+Smoke+Checklist (read-only link attached in the Jira ticket)
- JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWI-7832 (triage log + attachments)

We'll run the planned mitigations and provide a post-maintenance incident summary within 24 hours of completion. Thank you for coordinating Ops.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
